body:
**Assigned locations cannot be purged** When a location is assigned to a user, `purgeLocation` deletes the location without first removing its `user_location` row. This `RESTRICT` foreign key rejects the delete, so administrators cannot purge assigned locations. Remove the join rows during location purging or use the intended cascading behavior, and add coverage for purging an assigned location.
Artifacts
**[Evidence from the check](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/c9837d4e-2a17-44fb-8a36-89fada6f53ed)** - A Python SQLite harness creates the relevant schemas and executes the purge-equivalent DELETE in both states, showing the new RESTRICT foreign key blocks an assigned Location purge. **[Command output from the check](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/0e415bc4-4006-4f39-a471-fd917af47257)** - The executed before-schema run deletes Location 4 successfully and leaves zero Location rows, establishing the baseline. **[Command output from the check](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/bebf9b9d-b9f9-4208-9191-f82993e041a8)** - The executed after-migration run fails the Location DELETE with a foreign-key constraint error and leaves the Location and join row, confirming the defect. **[Command output from the check](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/11df5abc-5635-48f9-9710-c39d0cf5f8b2)** - The captured source inspection shows changed migration lines 168-171 use RESTRICT and the purge path directly removes the Location without join-row cleanup. **[Command output from the check](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/a449a759-18d5-42b6-8a5e-9dc1d0c47b2b)** - The attempted Maven API compile reports that JAVA\_HOME is not defined correctly, documenting why the actual Java source path could not be run in this environment.
Ran code and verified through T-Rex

**Getter violates empty-set contract** `getLocations()` promises an empty set for an unrestricted user, but a newly constructed `User` returns `null` because the field is not initialized. Callers that inspect or mutate the documented collection can therefore encounter a `NullPointerException`. This is non-blocking, but initializing the collection or returning an empty set avoids that practical cost. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

body: Fixed in 92c8b17c6: HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation now deletes the location's user_location rows before removing the location itself, so purging an assigned location no longer hits the RESTRICT FK.
Fixed in 92c8b17c6: User.locations is now initialized to an empty HashSet, so getLocations() returns empty rather than null for a fresh/unrestricted user, matching the documented contract.
Kindly could you add a regression test for the fix?

Added in 18ba36375: LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser assigns a location to a user then purges it, verifying the user_location row is cleaned up first and the FK no longer blocks the delete.

The native SQL `DELETE FROM user_location WHERE location_id = :locationId` bypasses Hibernate's session cache. If any future caller loads a user with `locations` before calling `purgeLocation`, the in-memory collection would be stale. Consider adding a comment or TODO noting this, or flush the session after the native delete. Safe in current code paths, so non-blocking.

Good catch — added a comment in 8a7e6fcdc noting the session-cache caveat and when to revisit it (evict/refresh or flush+clear), since you confirmed it's safe for current callers. Went with the comment over an unconditional flush to avoid changing flush timing/behavior for a case that doesn't exist yet.
